classification.difficultyReason: Translate displacement slopes into velocity graphs, coordinating turning points, changing steepness, flattening and the undefined derivative at a sharp corner.

inlines.text: Given the displacement-time graphs below, sketch the velocity-time graph.

spec.description: Downward displacement parabola through (0,0), (1,1) and (2,0), continuing downwards.
spec.mathematics: A possible exact model is x=2t-t^2 for t≥0.

answer.short: A decreasing straight line through $(0,2)$ and $(1,0)$, continuing below the $t$-axis.
answer.worked:
The gradient of the displacement graph decreases steadily. A matching displacement rule is $x(t)=2t-t^2$, so
$$\begin{align*}v(t)&=\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=2-2t.\end{align*}$$
Sketch this line, crossing the $t$-axis at $t=1$.

spec.description: Cubic-shaped displacement graph from (0,0), maximum (1,4), minimum (3,0), then rising.
spec.mathematics: The turning points are at t=1 and t=3.

answer.short: An upward-opening parabola crossing the $t$-axis at $t=1$ and $t=3$, with its minimum at $t=2$.
answer.worked: The displacement graph rises until $t=1$, falls until $t=3$, then rises again. Its gradients are zero at the two turning points. Sketch a positive velocity before $1$, a negative velocity between $1$ and $3$, and a positive velocity after $3$; the velocity curve has its minimum at $t=2$.

spec.description: Increasing displacement from (0,0), flattening towards dashed horizontal level x=2.
spec.mathematics: Displacement is increasing with positive gradient tending to zero.

answer.short: A positive velocity curve that decreases towards $0$ as $t$ increases.
answer.worked: The displacement keeps increasing, so its gradient and velocity are positive. The curve becomes flatter as it approaches $x=2$, so sketch the velocity decreasing towards $0$.

spec.description: Piecewise straight displacement graph from (0,0) to (1,1), then down through (2,0), continuing to the right.
spec.mathematics: Slope 1 before t=1 and slope -1 after t=1; sharp corner at t=1.

answer.short: $v=1$ for $0\leq t<1$ and $v=-1$ for $t>1$. Velocity is undefined at $t=1$.
answer.worked: The first straight segment has gradient $1$ and the second has gradient $-1$. Sketch horizontal velocity segments at those values. The displacement graph has a sharp corner at $t=1$, so there is no single instantaneous gradient there; use open endpoints.

spec.description: Horizontal velocity at 1 up to an open point at t=1; horizontal velocity at -1 after an open point at t=1.
spec.mathematics: v=1 on 0≤t<1, v=-1 on t>1; undefined at t=1.
